note: Ps55 betrayal by a friend (corrected; rich). Human IB core: prayer+supplication; restless complaint+moaning; the anguished heart, terrors of death, fear/trembling/horror; the dove-flight longing (fly-away+rest); the city's heaped corruption (violence/strife/iniquity/trouble/ruin/oppression/fraud); the betrayal grief (taunts he could bear, the equal/familiar-friend, sweet sod counsel) -> the treachery (stretched hand, violated covenant, smooth-butter speech but war-in-heart, softer-than-oil but drawn swords); the turn to trust (call, redeemed nefesh in shalom safety, cast-your-burden, 'I will trust'). God-qualifiers=12 (give-ear/attend/answer/hide-not to the prayer; save/hears/redeems/give-ear/sustain; imprecatory Destroy/divide/humble). Re-roled ~29 role-reassess mis-tags (human states + images + enemy traits). Every candidate roled.

dims.v: prayer (tefillah - give ear to my prayer)
begging God not to hide himself
paired with the plea for grace (supplication)
asking God to give ear and not hide (v1)

'Give ear to my PRAYER (tefillah), O God, and hide not yourself from my plea' — the opening cry of a man in extremity; tefillah the appeal that begs God's attention and dreads his silence, the anchor of the whole desperate psalm

'hide not yourself from my SUPPLICATION (techinnah)' — the plea for grace the psalmist casts on God; techinnah (appeal for favour) the humbled cry that expects nothing by right, only mercy — the posture beneath the prayer
be restless / roam in distress (rud - I am restless)

'I am RESTLESS (rud) in my complaint and I moan' — the agitated, wandering unrest of a tormented mind; rud (to roam/be restless) the inability to be still, the churning that drives the lament — inner turmoil that cannot settle
the complaint renewed evening, morning, noon (v17)
'restless in my COMPLAINT (siach)' — the outpoured lament; siach (musing/complaint) the voicing of the inner distress before God, kept up 'evening and morning and at noon' (v17) — grief given words
moan / be in commotion (hum - I moan)
'and I MOAN (hum)' — the wordless groaning of anguish; hum (to murmur/be in tumult) the inarticulate sound of a heart in commotion, beneath the spoken complaint — distress that overflows speech
wicked (rasha - the oppression of the wicked)
paired with the trouble they drop on him

'because of the noise of the enemy, the oppression of the WICKED (rasha)' — the hostile pressure that sets off the lament; rasha the godless foes whose clamour and oppression bear down on the psalmist
trouble / mischief (aven - they drop trouble on me)
'for they drop TROUBLE (aven) upon me' — the mischief the enemies heap on him; aven (iniquity/trouble) the harm they bring down, joined to their angry grudge — malice made active
anger (aph - in anger they bear a grudge)
paired with the grudge they cherish
'and in ANGER (aph) they bear a grudge against me' — the enemies' hot hostility; aph (nose/anger) the burning resentment out of which they cherish enmity — anger settled into grudge
the settled form of their anger
'they bear a GRUDGE (satam) against me' — the nursed, persistent enmity; satam (to cherish animosity) the anger that has hardened into a standing hatred — not a flash but a held resentment
heart (leb - my heart is in anguish)

'My HEART (leb) is in anguish within me' — the inner core convulsed; leb the seat of the whole inner life, here writhing under terror — the place where the betrayal and dread are felt (contrast the betrayer's war-filled heart, v21)
be in anguish / writhe (chul - my heart is in anguish)
paired with the terrors of death fallen on him
'my heart is in ANGUISH (chul)' — the writhing pain of the inner self; chul (to twist/writhe, as in birth-pangs) the acute torment of the heart, the physical figure of a soul in agony

'the TERRORS (emah) of death have fallen upon me' — dread of dying pressing in like a weight; emah (terror/dread) the death-fear that descends on the betrayed man, the deepest layer of his anguish, opening onto fear and trembling
fear / dread (yirah - fear and trembling come on me)

'FEAR (yirah) and trembling come upon me' — dread invading body and soul; yirah here not reverence but raw terror, the first of the triad (fear, trembling, horror) that engulfs the psalmist under the death-terrors
'fear and TREMBLING (raad) come upon me' — the body's share in the soul's dread; raad (shaking) the physical trembling that terror produces, the outward tremor of inward fear
the climax of fear and trembling

'and HORROR (pallatsuth) overwhelms me' — the shuddering that engulfs him wholly; pallatsuth (shuddering/horror) the climax of the dread-triad, covering him like a flood — terror that submerges the self and drives the longing to flee
fly away (uph - I would fly away)
to be at rest, far from the turmoil
paired with the longing to be at rest

'Oh that I had wings like a dove! I would FLY AWAY (uph) and be at rest' — the overwhelmed soul's yearning to escape; uph the wish for flight from unbearable turmoil, the instinct to flee rather than face the betrayal — longing for distance from the storm of the city
be at rest / settle (shakan - and be at rest)
long to rest / dwell in peace
the goal of the longed-for flight

'I would fly away and be at REST (shakan)' — the ache for peace, for a settled place away from strife; shakan (to dwell/settle) the repose the tormented heart craves — not mere escape but rest, the wilderness preferable to the treacherous city
violence (chamas - I see violence in the city)
paired with strife filling the city

'for I see VIOLENCE (chamas) and strife in the city' — the pervasive cruelty of the place; chamas (violent wrong) the first of the heaped-up civic sins (vv9-11), the wicked's disposition made the very air of the city
the psalmist asks God to destroy and confuse their tongues (v9)

'violence and STRIFE (rib) in the city' — the ceaseless contention among the wicked; rib (quarrel/dispute) the discord that the psalmist prays God will deepen by confusing their tongues (v9, the qualifier) — Babel as judgment on a divided, violent city
'INIQUITY (aven) and trouble are within it' — the wrong that dwells at the city's core; aven the iniquity that, with mischief, patrols the walls day and night — evil as the city's permanent resident
'iniquity and TROUBLE (amal) are within it' — the harmful toil the wicked inflict; amal (trouble/misery) the grievous mischief that fills the city, twin of iniquity — wrong that wearies and wounds
ruin / engulfing destruction (havvah - ruin in its midst)

'RUIN (havvah) is in its midst' — engulfing destruction at the city's heart; havvah (yawning ruin, cf Ps52) the devouring destructiveness that sits at the centre, from which oppression and fraud never depart

'OPPRESSION (tok) and fraud do not depart from its marketplace' — extortion woven into daily commerce; tok (oppression/injury) the crushing of the weak that, with fraud, never leaves the public square — sin as the city's economy
the same mirmah as the betrayer's treachery (v23)

'oppression and FRAUD (mirmah) do not depart' — the deceit that pervades the marketplace; mirmah (fraud/treachery) the lying that props up the oppression — the same word that names the betrayer's own treachery (v23), the city and the friend of one cloth
taunt / reproach (charaph - it is not an enemy who taunts)
the reproach he could have borne

'For it is not an enemy who TAUNTS (charaph) me — then I could bear it' — the reflection that sharpens the wound; charaph the reproach that from a known foe would be endurable — the pain is precisely that it comes from a friend, not an enemy
bear / endure (nasa - then I could bear it)
paired with hiding from an open adversary

'then I could BEAR (nasa) it' — the endurance that open enmity allows; nasa (to lift/carry) the capacity to shoulder a known foe's reproach — a strength that the betrayal of a friend dissolves, for there is no bracing against a trusted hand
one who hates / adversary (sane - not an adversary)

'it is not an ADVERSARY (sane, one who hates me) who deals insolently' — the open hater from whom one could hide; sane the declared enemy whose hostility is at least honest — the contrast that makes the friend's treachery unbearable
the act of the open adversary

'who DEALS INSOLENTLY (gadal) with me — then I could hide' — the open arrogance one could avoid; gadal (to make great/magnify oneself) the enemy's overt self-exalting, from which escape is possible — unlike the hidden dagger of a friend
hide oneself (sathar - then I could hide from him)
paired with bearing an enemy's taunt

'then I could HIDE (sathar) from him' — the refuge an open foe permits; sathar the self-concealment possible against a declared enemy — a defence the intimacy of a friend forecloses, since the betrayer was inside the guard
familiar friend / acquaintance (yada - my familiar friend)
a man his equal, his companion
the intimacy expressed in shared sweet counsel

'But it is you, a man my equal, my companion, my FAMILIAR FRIEND (yada)' — the identity of the betrayer that turns the knife; yada (one known/intimate) the trusted confidant, the depth of the bond that makes the treachery a wound no enemy could inflict
intimate counsel / close fellowship (sod - sweet counsel together)
sweet, walking to God's house in the throng
the closeness of the familiar friend

'We used to take sweet COUNSEL (sod) together' — the cherished intimacy now betrayed; sod (close confidence/secret shared) the trusting fellowship, deepened by worshipping together in God's house — the very sweetness of it measures the bitterness of the breach
evil (ra - evil is in their dwelling)
in their dwelling place, among them

'for EVIL (ra) is in their dwelling place, in their heart' — the wickedness lodged at the enemies' core; ra the evil that fills where they live — the ground of the imprecation that death surprise them, evil having made its home in them
call upon (qara - but I call to God)
the calling that the complaint sustains (v17)
and the LORD will save him (v16)

'But I CALL (qara) to God, and the LORD will save me' — the decisive turn from dread to trust; qara the psalmist's Godward cry, set against the treachery around him — the one recourse of the betrayed, confident that God will save (the qualifier)
complaint / musing (siach - I utter my complaint)
paired with moaning; renews the complaint of v2
and he hears the psalmist's voice (v17)

'Evening and morning and at noon I utter my COMPLAINT (siach) and moan' — persistent, rhythmed prayer; siach here the lament kept up through the whole day, and God hears his voice (the qualifier) — grief that does not despair but keeps addressing God
'I utter my complaint and MOAN (hamah)' — the groaning that accompanies the prayer; hamah (to murmur/be in commotion, cf v2) the sound of the heart's tumult, kept up before the God who hears
paired with the safety in which it is redeemed
God redeems it from the battle he wages (v18)

'He redeems my SOUL (nefesh) in safety from the battle that I wage' — the endangered life brought out unharmed; nefesh here the psalmist's self, redeemed (the qualifier) into peace though many war against him — the soul rescued whole
the peace in which the soul is redeemed

'he redeems my soul in SAFETY (shalom)' — the wholeness/peace of the rescued self; shalom here the unharmed security into which God brings the soul out of battle — peace as the fruit of redemption, the opposite of the war in the betrayer's heart (v21)
do not change / will not repent
paired with their not fearing God

'because they do not CHANGE (chaliphah) and do not fear God' — the moral fixity of the wicked; chaliphah (change/turning) here the refusal to alter course, obstinacy in evil — an unrepentance rooted in having no fear of God
paired with their refusal to change
so God will give ear and humble them (v19)

'and do not FEAR (yare) God' — the fearlessness that is the root of their obstinacy; yare here the reverent fear of God the enemies lack — the same godlessness as the ruthless (Ps54) and the fool (Ps53), which draws God's humbling (the qualifier)
stretch out (the hand) (shalach - stretched out his hand against his friends)
against those at peace with him

'My companion STRETCHED OUT (shalach) his hand against those at peace with him' — the raised hand of the traitor; shalach here the act of aggression against one's own allies — betrayal turned to open violence, the hand that had shared bread now lifted to strike
profane / violate (chalal - he violated his covenant)
paired with the hand stretched against friends

'he VIOLATED (chalal) his covenant' — the sacred bond profaned; chalal (to profane/pollute) the treachery of breaking a sworn covenant of friendship — faithlessness at its most defiling, the trust desecrated
smooth / slippery (chalaq - his speech was smooth)
set against the war hidden in his heart

'His speech was SMOOTH (chalaq) as butter, yet war was in his heart' — the deceptive surface of the traitor; chalaq (smooth/flattering) the oily plausibility of his words, a pleasant exterior masking hostility — the split between voice and heart that defines treachery
war / conflict (qerab - war was in his heart)
the reality beneath the smooth speech

'yet WAR (qerab) was in his heart' — the true, hostile interior; qerab (battle) the enmity concealed in the traitor's heart while his mouth ran smooth — the definitive exposure: outward peace, inward war
heart (leb - war was in his heart)
the seat that hides war behind smooth words

'war was in his HEART (leb)' — the traitor's inner core as a battlefield; leb here the hidden seat where hostility is nursed while the mouth flatters — the dark mirror of the psalmist's own anguished heart (v4), one bleeding, the other plotting
soft / smooth (rakak - words softer than oil)
softer than oil, yet drawn swords

'his words were SOFTER (rakak) than oil, yet they were drawn swords' — the gentlest speech hiding the sharpest intent; rakak (to be soft/tender) the smoothness of his words, exposed as concealed blades — deceit that weaponises tenderness
cast / throw (shalak - cast your burden on the LORD)
paired with the righteous kept from being moved

'CAST (shalak) your burden on the LORD, and he will sustain you' — the counsel of trust wrung from the ordeal; shalak here the deliberate act of throwing one's care onto God, releasing what one cannot carry — trust as a decision, answered by God's sustaining (the qualifier)
righteous (tsaddiq - never permit the righteous to be moved)
the one who casts his burden on God

'he will never permit the RIGHTEOUS (tsaddiq) to be moved' — the settled security of the God-truster; tsaddiq the upright one whom God keeps unshaken — the promised stability that answers the psalm's terror, the opposite of the betrayers who will not live out half their days
treachery / deceit (mirmah - men of blood and treachery)
the same mirmah as the city's fraud (v11) and betrayer's ways

'men of blood and TREACHERY (mirmah) shall not live out half their days' — the deceit that marks the doomed; mirmah (treachery/fraud) the defining trait of the bloody men, the same word as the city's fraud (v11) — their treachery cuts short their own days
trust (batach - but I will trust in you)
the closing counterpart to casting one's burden on God (v22)

'But I will TRUST (batach) in you' — the psalm's final resolution; batach the deliberate resting in God that closes the turmoil — over against the treacherous who trust their own violence, the betrayed man plants himself on God alone
give ear (azan - give ear to my prayer)
God's attending asked of the prayer (v1)
v1 QUALIFIER (God's act asked): 'GIVE EAR (azan) to my prayer, O God' - God's listening is not a human IB char; the attention the psalmist's prayer (280027) seeks. Qualifier.
God's hiding (dreaded, negated) from the plea (v1)
v1 QUALIFIER (God's act, negated): 'HIDE (alam) not yourself from my plea' - God's self-hiding is not a human IB char; the divine silence the prayer (280027) dreads and begs against. Qualifier.
attend / pay heed (qashab - attend to me)
God's heeding asked of the prayer (v2)
v2 QUALIFIER (God's act asked): 'ATTEND (qashab) to me, and answer me' - God's heeding is not a human IB char; the notice the prayer (280027) begs. Qualifier.
God's answering asked of the prayer (v2)
v2 QUALIFIER (God's act asked): 'and ANSWER (anah) me' - God's response is not a human IB char; the reply the prayer (280027) awaits. Qualifier.
destroy / swallow up (bala - Destroy, O Lord)
God's destroying asked upon the city's strife (v9)

v9 QUALIFIER (God's act asked): 'DESTROY (bala), O Lord, divide their tongues' - God's judgment is not a human IB char; the imprecation the psalmist prays against the violence and strife (280207) of the city. Qualifier.
God's confusing of their speech asked against their strife (v9)

v9 QUALIFIER (God's act asked): 'DIVIDE (palag) their tongues' - God's confusing of their speech (a Babel-judgment) is not a human IB char; asked against the strife (280207) that fills the city. Qualifier.
save (yasha - the LORD will save me)
God's saving, the confidence of the one who calls (v16)
v16 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'and the LORD will SAVE (yasha) me' - God's saving is not a human IB char; the deliverance the psalmist's calling (280085) counts on. Qualifier.
v17 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'and he HEARS (shama) my voice' - God's hearing is not a human IB char; the divine response that meets the complaint (280094) kept up evening, morning, and noon. Qualifier.
redeem / ransom (padah - he redeems my soul)
God redeems the psalmist's soul in safety (v18)

v18 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'He REDEEMS (padah) my soul in safety from the battle' - God's redeeming is not a human IB char; the rescue that brings the nefesh (280100) out whole though many war against him. Qualifier.
hear / give ear (shama - God will give ear)
God gives ear and, enthroned of old, humbles the enemies (v19)

v19 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'God will GIVE EAR (shama) and humble them, he who is enthroned from of old' - God's hearing/responding is not a human IB char; the divine attention that answers the complaint (280094) and brings the wicked low. Qualifier.
God humbles the enemies who do not fear him (v19)

v19 QUALIFIER (God's act, re-roled from an earlier mis-call): 'and HUMBLE (anah) them' - God's afflicting of the enemies is not a human IB char; the judgment on those who do not fear God (280118). Qualifier.
sustain / hold up (kul - he will sustain you)
God sustains the one who casts his burden on him (v22)
v22 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'and he will SUSTAIN (kul) you' - God's upholding is not a human IB char; the divine support promised to the one who casts his burden on the LORD (280143). Qualifier.
oppression / pressure (aqah - the oppression of the wicked)
v3: 'the OPPRESSION (aqah) of the wicked' - the external pressure the enemies exert; the wicked's disposition is the char (280173), here the harm/pressure itself. Standalone (external pressure).
bring down / drop (mut - they drop trouble on me)
v3: 'they DROP (mut) trouble upon me' - the enemies' act of casting trouble down; the harm itself is the char (280176), here the bare act of inflicting. Standalone (hostile act).
v4: 'the terrors of DEATH (mavet)' - death as the object/source of the dread; the terror is the char (280184), here the thing feared. Standalone.
v4: 'the terrors of death have FALLEN (naphal) upon me' - the descent of the terrors; the dread itself is the char (280184), here the manner of its coming (falling like a weight). Standalone.
v5: 'horror OVERWHELMS (kasah) me' - the covering/engulfing of the horror; the horror is the char (280192), here the manner of its overwhelming. Standalone.
v6: 'Oh that I had wings like a DOVE (yonah)!' - the image of the escaping bird; the flight-longing is the char (306384), here the picture that carries it. Standalone (image).
wander / flee (nadad - I would wander far away)
v7: 'I would WANDER (nadad) far away' - a further verb of the flight-longing (306384); the desire to distance himself from the turmoil. Standalone (flight expression).
be far / go far off (rachaq - wander far away)
v7: 'I would wander FAR AWAY (rachaq)' - the distancing that the flight-longing (306384) seeks; the far remove from the treacherous city. Standalone (flight expression).
lodge / spend the night (lin - lodge in the wilderness)
v7: 'I would LODGE (lin) in the wilderness' - the longing to shelter far off; the wilderness preferred to the city, an expression of the flight-longing (306384). Standalone (flight expression).
hurry / hasten (chush - I would hurry to find shelter)
v8: 'I would HURRY (chush) to find a shelter' - the urgency of the flight-longing (306384); the haste to reach refuge from the storm. Standalone (flight expression).
shelter / place of escape (miflat - a shelter)
v8: 'a SHELTER (miflat) from the raging wind and tempest' - the refuge sought; the image of safety the flight-longing (306384) aims at. Standalone (image).
v8: 'from the RAGING (saah) wind and tempest' - the fury of the storm imaged; the turmoil the psalmist would flee (the strife of the city), a picture, not an inner operation. Standalone (image).
v8: 'the raging WIND (ruach) and tempest' - the storm-wind as image of the surrounding turmoil; here ruach = wind/storm (not spirit), a picture of the violence fled. Standalone (image).
v8: 'the raging wind and TEMPEST (saar)' - the storm imaging the city's strife the psalmist longs to escape; a picture, not an inner operation. Standalone (image).
go around / patrol (sabab - they go around it on the walls)

v10: 'Day and night they GO AROUND (sabab) it on its walls' - the personified sins/violence patrolling the city; the prowling motion of the corruption named in the sin-chars (violence, iniquity, etc.). Standalone (personified motion).

v11: 'oppression and fraud do not DEPART (mush) from its marketplace' - the permanence of the sins; the wickedness itself is the char (oppression 280043, fraud 280044), here its refusal to leave. Standalone (permanence).
equal / of like value (erek - a man my equal)

v13: 'a man my EQUAL (erek), my companion' - the betrayer's status as the psalmist's peer; the intimacy is the char (familiar friend 280066), here the bare equality of rank that deepens the wound. Standalone (relational status).

v14: 'We used to take SWEET (mathaq) counsel together' - the sweetness that qualified the shared intimacy (280068); the pleasantness of the fellowship, carried in the counsel char's manner. Standalone (quality of the fellowship).
throng / festal crowd (regesh - walked in the throng)

v14: 'within God's house we walked in the THRONG (regesh)' - the festal crowd going up to worship; the setting of the betrayed intimacy, an external procession, not an inner operation. Standalone (setting).
death (mavet - let death steal over them)
v15: 'Let DEATH (mavet) steal over them' - death invoked upon the enemies in the imprecation; the fate called down, not an inner operation. Standalone.
come deceitfully / seize by surprise (nasha - let death steal over them)

v15: 'let death STEAL (nasha) over them' - the manner of the invoked death (coming upon them by surprise/deceitfully); part of the imprecation, the way death is called to seize them. Standalone (manner of the fate invoked).
Sheol / the grave (sheol - go down to Sheol alive)
v15: 'let them go down to SHEOL (sheol) alive' - the grave as the destination invoked (echoing Korah's fate); the place of the imprecated judgment, not an inner operation. Standalone.
battle / war (qerab - the battle that I wage)

v18: 'in safety from the BATTLE (qerab) that I wage' - the external conflict the psalmist is embroiled in; the soul's rescue from it is the char (280100), here the battle itself. Standalone (external conflict).
those at peace / allies (shalom - against his friends)

v20: 'stretched out his hand against those at peace (shalom) with him' - the covenant partners/allies the betrayer attacked; the victims of the treachery, its object (the assault is the char, 280126). Standalone (the peace-partners).
v20: 'he violated his COVENANT (berit)' - the sworn bond the betrayer broke; the violating is the char (280130), here the covenant itself, the object profaned. Standalone (the bond broken).
v21: 'his speech was smooth as BUTTER (chemah)' - the simile for the traitor's smooth speech (280134); the deceptive-surface image, not an inner operation. Standalone (image).
v21: 'his words were softer than OIL (shemen)' - the simile for the smoothness of the traitor's words (280139); the soothing-surface image, not an inner operation. Standalone (image).
drawn swords (petichah - yet they were drawn swords)

v21: 'yet they were DRAWN SWORDS (petichah)' - the image of the true, hostile nature beneath the soft words; the concealed violence (the inner war is the char 280136), here the picture of words-as-blades. Standalone (image of hidden violence).
v22: 'Cast your BURDEN (yehav) on the LORD' - the care/lot to be entrusted to God; the casting is the char (280143), here the burden itself, its object. Standalone (the care cast).
be moved / shaken (mot - never permit the righteous to be moved)

v22: 'he will never permit the righteous to be MOVED (mot)' - the shaking (negated) that God prevents; the security of the righteous is the char (280151), here the being-shaken that is denied. Standalone (negated shaking).
destruction / the pit (shachath - pit of destruction)
v23: 'you will cast them down into the pit of DESTRUCTION (shachath)' - the pit of ruin as the enemies' fate; the destination of God's judgment, not an inner operation. Standalone.
v23: 'men of BLOOD (dam) and treachery' - the bloodguilt marking the enemies; their treachery is the char (280161), here the bloodshed that names them. Standalone (bloodguilt descriptor).
half / divide (chatsah - not live out half their days)
v23: 'shall not live out HALF (chatsah) their days' - the shortened lifespan of the bloody and treacherous; the outcome of God's judgment on them, not an inner operation. Standalone (fate).
